attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as a NAT gateway on its eth1 interface (10.50.50.254/24, the private network shared with node2/node3), with a source-NAT masquerade rule translating 10.50.50.0/24 traffic out eth0 to the internet. node2 (10.50.50.11) and node3 (10.50.50.12) were given static eth1 addresses and a secondary default route via node1 (metric 200, below the pre-existing eth0 control-plane default), plus rp_filter=0 on eth1 to stop strict reverse-path filtering from dropping asymmetric replies (the only real bug found, confirmed via tcpdump). End-to-end verified via eth1-bound ping and HTTPS from both node2 and node3, with tcpdump on node1 showing correct request/reply masquerade translation between eth1 and eth0. Then performed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes: captured baseline boot_id and health, rebooted each node individually, polled until exec was available again, confirmed boot_id changed, and re-verified NAT config, routes, rp_filter setting, and live internet connectivity through node1 after each restart. All three nodes recovered fully with persisted configuration.
